query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a large fraction of Pt (around 50 at.%) into an equiatomic FeCoNi high‐entropy alloy, followed by a rapid thermal annealing step to trigger L10 ordering, will convert its structure from soft fcc to a lower-symmetry intermetallic phase with enhanced magnetic anisotropy and substantially higher coercivity compared to the baseline.
generation.material_initial_state: A single-phase, fcc FeCoNi alloy having high saturation magnetization and low coercivity.
generation.intervention: Alloy the system by replacing roughly half of the typical metal content with Pt (i.e., produce a near-equiatomic FeCoNiPt composition that still maintains an overall high configurational entropy of approximately ≥ 1.0R), and then apply rapid thermal annealing to induce an L10 ordered phase.
generation.conditions: The alloy must be prepared as a multicomponent (near equiatomic) high-entropy system and processed under conditions (e.g., thin film deposition or bulk processing with rapid thermal annealing) that enable atomic ordering. The Pt concentration and annealing parameters must be chosen to promote symmetry breaking (L10 ordering) without causing phase separation that would compromise the high entropy criterion.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a single, ordered L10 phase (with tetragonal symmetry) induced by Pt addition and thermal processing.
generation.mechanism: Pt, with its strong spin–orbit coupling, reduces the lattice symmetry when it is alloyed in, thus promoting the L10 ordering. This lower symmetry increases magnetocrystalline anisotropy and facilitates enhanced domain wall pinning, leading to a significant increase in coercivity relative to the soft magnetic fcc state of pure FeCoNi.
generation.predicted_outcome: The resulting FeCoNiPt high-entropy alloy is predicted to exhibit a coercivity increase by at least an order of magnitude over the original soft fcc FeCoNi baseline, though its saturation magnetization may be moderately reduced.
generation.baseline: The as-deposited or as-cast fcc FeCoNi alloy with high saturation magnetization and low coercivity.
generation.boundary: This effect is expected only when the Pt fraction and rapid thermal annealing conditions are optimized to induce L10 ordering while retaining the high-entropy multicomponent nature. Exceeding the Pt concentration significantly or using insufficient thermal processing may either lower the configurational entropy too much or fail to produce the desired ordered phase, respectively.
generation.uncertainty: While similar Pt-induced ordering in other HEA thin films (as in PMC11426066) supports this approach, the precise quantitative enhancement of coercivity and the sensitivity to processing parameters (e.g., exact Pt content and annealing time/temperature) remain to be optimized.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: a control group of single-phase fcc FeCoNi and an experimental group of near-equiatomic FeCoNiPt designed to achieve L10 ordering. Apply identical processing steps except that the experimental group undergoes rapid thermal annealing under conditions optimized for ordering. Use X-ray diffraction (XRD) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to confirm the formation of the L10 phase, and measure the magnetic hysteresis loops (e.g., via vibrating-sample magnetometry or SQUID magnetometry) to determine coercivity and saturation magnetization.
measurements: XRD for phase identification and detection of L10 ordering
Magnetic hysteresis measurements to quantify coercivity and saturation magnetization
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Pt-doped, annealed samples do not exhibit clear evidence of L10 ordering or if their measured coercivity fails to increase by at least an order of magnitude (relative to the fcc FeCoNi baseline), then the hypothesis is considered falsified.

Single‐Phase L10‐Ordered High Entropy Thin Films with High Magnetic Anisotropy

Abstract: AbstractThe vast high entropy alloy (HEA) composition space is promising for discovery of new material phases with unique properties. This study explores the potential to achieve rare‐earth‐free high magnetic anisotropy materials in single‐phase HEA thin films. Thin films of FeCoNiMnCu sputtered on thermally oxidized Si/SiO2 substrates at room temperature are magnetically soft, with a coercivity on the order of 10 Oe. After post‐deposition rapid thermal annealing (RTA), the films exhibit a single face‐centered‐cubic phase, with an almost 40‐fold increase in coercivity. Inclusion of 50 at.% Pt in the film leads to ordering of a single L10 high entropy intermetallic phase after RTA, along with high magnetic anisotropy and 3 orders of magnitude coercivity increase. Magnetically-driven phase transformation strengthening in high entropy alloys

Abstract: AbstractCrCoNi alloy exhibits a remarkable combination of strength and plastic deformation, even superior to the CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy. We connect the magnetic and mechanical properties of CrCoNi, via a magnetically tunable phase transformation. While both alloys crystallize as single-phase face-centered-cubic (fcc) solid solutions, we find a distinctly lower-energy phase in CrCoNi alloy with a hexagonal close-packed (hcp) structure. Comparing the magnetic configurations of CrCoNi with those of other equiatomic ternary derivatives of CrMnFeCoNi confirms that magnetically frustrated Mn eliminates the fcc-hcp energy difference. This highlights the unique combination of chemistry and magnetic properties in CrCoNi, leading to a fcc-hcp phase transformation that occurs only in this alloy, and is triggered by dislocation slip and interaction with internal boundaries. This phase transformation sets CrCoNi apart from the parent quinary, and its other equiatomic ternary derivatives, and provides a new way for increasing strength without compromising plastic deformation. Influence of Cr Substitution and Temperature on Hierarchical Phase Decomposition in the AlCoFeNi High Entropy Alloy

Abstract: While the AlCoFeNi high entropy alloy exhibits a single ordered B2 phase at high temperature, both the substitution of ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr, and lower annealing temperatures lead to a tendency for this system to decompose into a two-phase mixture of ordered B2 and disordered BCC solid solution. The length scale of this decomposition is determined by the combination of composition and annealing temperature, as demonstrated in this investigation by comparing and contrasting AlCoFeNi with the AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi alloy. The resulting phase stability has been rationalized based on solution thermodynamic predictions. Additionally, it is shown that replacement of Co by Cr in the AlCoFeNi alloy resulted in a substantial reduction in saturation magnetization and increase in coercivity. The microhardness is also strongly influenced by the composition and the length scale of B2 + BCC decomposition in these high entropy alloys.
